answer: Endorsement travels across a cut in the endorsement graph, and a cut is only real when the two sides have no common ancestor inside the endorsement horizon, so a cluster must be dissolved and rebuilt before its weight counts elsewhere. This cost is per identity, so it cannot be amortised across the fleet. The velvet is the island, the zenith the endorsement that crosses it, and the spiral the shared ancestor that would disqualify the crossing; one velvet is cheap to hold, but a zenith only counts when no spiral exists, and that takes independent history.
